Texas ramping the ultra-high-power CW laser for CPO (incl. the NVIDIA partnership), revenue from the DECEMBER quarter. CPO+NPO+integrated optics = >$15bn incremental TAM; CONTENT PER SOCKET COMPARABLE for CPO vs NPO ('just a different attach point'). Engagement intensity up sharply over the last 3-6 months — almost every large strategic customer has a CPO and/or NPO project. New PhotonLink full-stack integrated-optics platform unveiled at ECOC (launch 09-21-2026), first revenue Dec quarter. CPO for SCALE-UP revenue starts 2H CY2027; 200G VCSEL targeted at NPO (Coherent Q4 FY2026)

Corning fiber-content framework — full-optical scale-up = 160 FIBERS/GPU (14.4Tbps/200G x2 + 16 scale-out) = 10x today's scale-out-only 16; Vera Rubin Ultra NVL576 = HYBRID (copper in-rack, optical rack-to-rack); >130k-GPU clusters need a 3rd optical layer (+50% content); content/GPU +1.3-1.5x by 2028; new PHOTONICS map (inside-the-box passives incl FAU) targets $10B by 2030 (Corning Q2 FY2026)

FormFactor - CPO test revenue ACCELERATING AHEAD OF PLAN: 2026 guide raised from $10-20M to 'significantly exceed $20M', with >$20M already expected by end-Q3; systems segment a record $48.5M (+74% QoQ) largely on CPO. Leadership in INSERTION 1 (known-good-die on the PIC wafer before it is combined with the EIC to form the optical module for scale-up/scale-out switches); served market ~$400M by 2030; revenue recognized through the leading foundry (11% customer) (FormFactor Q2 FY2026)
Credo closes Dust Photonics (SiPho PICs, 800G/1.6T -> 3.2T+, fewer lasers); CPO/NPO initial revenue expected FY2028
Veeco — >$250M multi-product orders (MOCVD/wet/IBD) for INDIUM PHOSPHIDE laser manufacturing; deliveries 2026, accelerating 2027 (copper->optics transition) (Veeco Q1 FY2026)

Semtech — 1.6T FiberEdge ramp STARTS; >50% share of 1.6T FiberEdge targeted by Jan-2027; 1.6T (FiberEdge+CopperEdge) >50% of data-center revenue in Q3-26; photonics portfolio (gain chip / high-power CW laser / SOA / PD array) targets $80-90 content per transceiver at 3.2T; engaged on 10-15 MPO/NPO programs with module makers (Semtech Q2 FY2027)
Keysight — 1.6T physical-layer test with 20+ industry leaders at OFC; first public Ultra Ethernet Consortium interop demo with Broadcom; 3.2T R&D rising (Keysight Q2 FY2026)
BESI/ASMPT view — next-gen GPU (2028) 3D stacking forecast to be HYBRID BONDED; CPO equipment TAM inflects (orders 2026, install 2027)

Viavi (test) - CPO revenue ALREADY STARTING (Sept qtr, accelerating in December) and yield-slippage talk rejected: 'that's all nonsense... I have POs to show for that'. Yield management INCREASES test intensity (known-good die / known-good optical engine / known-good substrate), taking Viavi into 'the optical plane of the semiconductor test - a completely new market'. Why CPO happens at all: 'your THREE NANOMETER SILICON PERFORMS AS A TWO NANOMETER SILICON - almost a whole node of advantage by co-packaging the optics' (Viavi Q4 FY2026)

Applied Optoelectronics - CPO laser physics sized: ELSFP needs a 300mW laser vs 70mW (800G) / 100mW (1.6T) with ~6x larger die, so the INDUSTRY LASER MARKET MUST GROW 8-10x to serve CPO; next-gen ELSFP moves to DWDM where yield loss is 40-50% worse than 1310nm, and laser equipment runs 21-24 MONTHS from order to high volume. AOI engaged with ~5 CPO customers on 3-4 year demand and already qualified by several on fixed-wavelength CPO laser/ELSFP; HIGH-VOLUME ELSFP only from late Q3-2027, reaching ~400k pcs/month in 2028. Houston laser fab +~300% capacity by Q3-2027 plus a second fab cleanroom ~4x the current one. AOI is absent from FIRST-GEN CPO deployments purely because laser output must feed its own transceivers first. Margins: laser 55-65%, ELSFP module >50%. China seen 2-3+ years from a 300mW DWDM CPO laser (AAOI Q2 FY2026)

tables.title: Latest graph signals (auto-derived)
rows: MARKET / ROADMAP DATA POINTS: 800G transceiver INDUSTRY volume went from ~20 MILLION UNITS/YEAR two years ago to ~90 MILLION UNITS/YEAR this year — the industry entered the year forecasting 50M units and Semtech is 'now hearing the number 80, 90 million'; 800G bookings are still INCREASING (not decreasing), and 800G and 1.6T both have 'a really very healthy runway over the next two years'. 3.2T TIMING: design window starts opening in ~12 MONTHS, EARLY MOVERS ~18 MONTHS OUT, MEANINGFUL DEPLOYMENT IN ~2 YEARS (i.e. H2 CY2028) — that is the cut-in for Semtech's content step-up, and above 200G/lane is where TIA + photodiode CO-OPTIMIZATION becomes necessary. MPO/NPO called a strong trend driven by BANDWIDTH-DENSITY limits against fixed shoreline: Semtech is engaged on '10, 15 DIFFERENT PROGRAMS' with module manufacturers, some tied directly to end customers, as a leading supplier of TIA ARRAYS and (linearized) LASER ARRAYS; higher density tightens element spacing and crosstalk, changing packaging requirements. LPO has generated meaningful revenue since Q1 FY2027 and is growing moderately, but its bigger effect is PROVING THE LINEAR ARCHITECTURE, which now carries into MPO, XPO and 'some form of CPO'. Stated R&D priority: lasers, photodiodes, drivers and TIAs for 3.2T coherent light, XPO, MPO and CPO applications. Analyst day 10-15-2026 (San Jose) will publish TAM, share and the multi-year model.
800G industry units ~20M/yr (2024) → ~90M/yr (2026); 3.2T volume ~2 years out; 10-15 MPO/NPO programs

CO-PACKAGED OPTICS: ADI views the nascent CPO space as a SAM EXPANDER - the criticality of its precision control technology increases further as THERMAL AND SERVICEABILITY challenges rise in co-packaged architectures. Combined with market growth, expanding content and increasing share, management says data center optics will remain a strong growth vector for ADI over the coming years.
CPO framed as SAM expander; no specific figure

Optical speed transitions are running CONCURRENTLY rather than sequentially - 'pretty unprecedented... 800G is still sort of the underlying technology, but 1.6T is scaling, and typically that would have been spaced out a little more'. Transceiver manufacturers are RAPIDLY SCALING 800G AND 1.6T optical transceivers on Keysight's industry-leading 224G digital communication analyzers, and customers are 'ramping production of 1.6T as we speak right now' with very strong demand - Q4 wireline mix is expected to tilt further toward PRODUCTION test as a result. Customers are ALREADY ENGAGING KEYSIGHT ON 3.2T (demo run at a conference earlier this year). Optical component ecosystem investment continues to ramp and key players are adopting the lab portfolio including the INDUSTRY'S FIRST 220 GHz LIGHTWAVE COMPONENT ANALYZER, introduced at OFC this year. Wireline R&D-vs-manufacturing mix has shifted from ~80/20 historically to ~70/30 and roughly two-thirds / one-third over the last couple of quarters.
800G+1.6T scaling concurrently on 224G DCAs; 3.2T engagements live; first 220GHz LCA

CPO and NPO positioning: NPO (near-packaged optics) sits between pluggable modules and CPO, and Fabrinet believes it is positioned to be the leader in manufacturing and packaging NPO devices given tens of millions of pluggables built plus CPO work already underway with a handful of customers (building devices, not yet at full-scale volumes). Seamus Grady: NPO 'probably represents a more near-term opportunity than CPO from what we have seen with our customers,' and as NPO scales to 6.4T, 12.8T and beyond, manufacturing complexity and yield become critical. Revenue and margin from these programs are too early to quantify. The Raytek partnership is described as instrumental to unlocking the demand, and Raytek will add capacity in Thailand on Fabrinet's own campus so all required packaging capability sits under one roof.
NPO scaling to 6.4T/12.8T; CPO work with a handful of customers, not yet full-scale volume

→ Raytec Semiconductor: Fabrinet recorded an approximately $56.7 million non-cash gain from remeasuring its investment in Raytek, and will treat future remeasurement gains or losses the same way. Strategically, Raytek will add capacity in Thailand ON FABRINET'S OWN CAMPUS so that all packaging capability required for CPO and NPO products sits under one roof, either in Fabrinet's production lines or in partnership with Raytek. Management calls the partnership 'instrumental in allowing us to unlock the potential of the demand we are seeing.'
value: $56.7M non-cash remeasurement gain on the existing ~14% stake

Raytek (Raytec Semiconductor) will add wafer-level packaging capacity in Thailand ON FABRINET'S CAMPUS, so that the full set of packaging capabilities required for CPO and NPO devices sits under one roof - either in Fabrinet's own production lines or in partnership with Raytek. Fabrinet also recorded an approximately $56.7 million non-cash gain remeasuring its existing ~14% investment in Raytek in fiscal Q4 2026.
$56.7M non-cash remeasurement gain on Fabrinet's ~14% stake; new Thailand capacity on Fabrinet's campus

FY2027 framed as a significant acceleration: having just delivered its first $2B revenue quarter, Coherent expects its FIRST QUARTER ABOVE $3B OF REVENUE BY THE END OF FISCAL 2027, with EPS again growing significantly faster than revenue. Confidence rests on three stated factors: (1) record bookings again in Q4 with demand still growing, (2) rising supply of critical components led by the indium phosphide doubling, and (3) multiple new revenue streams ramping — optical circuit switching, co-packaged optics, multi-rail systems, and advanced materials for data-center thermal and power management. Data center and communications was 79% of total Q4 revenue.
first >$3B revenue quarter targeted by end of FY2027; DC+comms = 79% of revenue

Integrated optics: CPO, NPO and other forms represent MORE THAN $15 BILLION of incremental addressable market. At ECOC in September (launch event September 21) Coherent unveils COHERENT PHOTONLINK, a complete integrated-optics platform spanning the full optical signal chain — light generation, beam shaping, transmission, detection and conversion back to an electrical signal for the XPU or switch chip — supporting CPO, NPO and other optical integration. Initial PhotonLink-related revenue begins in the DECEMBER QUARTER. Engagement intensity with customers on CPO and/or NPO 'has really gone up over the last three to six months', with almost every large strategic customer running a CPO or NPO project (some both). Content per socket is COMPARABLE between CPO and NPO — 'just a different attach point' — because Coherent supplies the laser, external laser module, isolators, polarization-maintaining fiber, full fiber-attach kit assembly and SiPho PICs rather than a single ingredient. CPO for SCALE-UP applications starts generating revenue in the second half of calendar 2027; the CPO ramping now goes first into scale-out. The 200G VCSEL is expected to be adopted in NPO/integrated-optics applications.
integrated optics >$15B incremental TAM; PhotonLink unveiled Sept 21, first revenue Dec quarter; CPO scale-up revenue 2H CY2027

Potential U.S. import restrictions on optical transceivers (a Reuters report management called speculative) would benefit Coherent as 'the largest U.S. supplier of transceivers'. Coherent has OVER 20 PRODUCTION FACILITIES IN THE U.S., including Sherman, Texas, which makes critical components for transceivers AND for CPO/NPO applications, plus U.S. sites producing fiber optic cable and growing the garnet used in transceiver isolators. Management said it would be open to increasing U.S. manufacturing further, and confirmed that a number of customers have since reached out to discuss manufacturing options — 'that has spurred some new customer demand and supply discussions.' Separately, Coherent does not expect to sell indium phosphide lasers externally in the near future because data-center transceiver demand absorbs every bit of capacity 'and then some'.
>20 U.S. production facilities; possible import restrictions spurring new customer supply discussions

→ NVIDIA: The Texas facility HAS BEGUN RAMPING the ultra-high-power CW laser for CPO solutions, 'including those covered by our NVIDIA partnership', with revenue expected to begin ramping in fiscal Q2 (the December quarter). Management reported NO push-out of CPO demand — the opposite: 'we have seen demand increase and request from customers' demand getting pulled in.'

CPO / ultra-high-power lasers: lead CPO customers' production plans 'remain very much on track, and their demand signal has increased since our last update.' Lumentum remains confident in an ultra-high-power laser chip demand ramp in the second half of calendar 2027, ahead of customer scale-up deployments in calendar 2028. Because the first phase of scale-up optical connections spans across compute racks within a cluster, the ramp applies to any topology larger than one rack. Ultra-high-power laser revenue is expected to reach roughly the $50 million mark by the end of calendar 2026, with the first triple-digit ($100M+) quarter expected in fiscal Q3 FY2027.
UHP laser ramp H2 CY2027 for CY2028 scale-up; ~$50M by end CY2026; first $100M+ quarter fiscal Q3 FY2027

First external light source (ELS) MODULE purchase order received, for delivery by the second half of calendar 2027 - Lumentum's first move up the stack from selling laser chips into selling the full ELS module. ASP is 'meaningfully higher than the set of lasers that we ship in'; module margins are above corporate average but below the laser chips, a deliberate trade of some margin for revenue acceleration. Wupen Yuen: the ELS module is positioned to enable 'customers who don't know how to deal with individual laser chips' to build CPO and NPO systems.
first ELS module purchase order (delivery H2 CY2027); ASP meaningfully higher than laser set

NPO (near-packaged optics) called 'completely additive' and 'significantly increasing the optical TAM.' The rest of the customer base beyond the lead CPO account is prioritizing NPO as an intermediate step to eventual CPO adoption; even the largest CPO customer is evaluating NPO for specific new use cases. Two laser types are being evaluated for NPO: a mid-power laser integrated directly into the optical engine, and a high-power laser in an external light source module. Lumentum's NPO/CPO laser family spans 120 mW, 150 mW, and 400 mW output levels off common design and process know-how. Wupen Yuen: each NPO set carries ~6.4T of bandwidth, roughly four times a local module, and NPO should hit the market in the late 2027 / 2028 timeframe to enable optical scale-up.
NPO additive to optical TAM; 120/150/400 mW laser family; ~6.4T per NPO set; market late 2027-2028

Technology roadmap view: silicon photonics is a viable solution at 1.6T and CW lasers are taking a significant portion of transceiver output, but at 3.2T silicon photonics 'loses some of its advantages' and Lumentum expects EMLs to come back in a meaningful way. Wupen Yuen added that in a supply-constrained environment customers will use whichever laser source they can get, so the EML-versus-CW mix is a supply/demand dynamic as much as a technical one. CPO remains the natural end state - optics placed directly on the substrate or interposer for maximum power efficiency through foundry-level advanced packaging.
SiPho viable at 1.6T; EML expected to return at 3.2T; CPO the end state via foundry advanced packaging

Networking is now an explicit DCBBS pillar: the total solution spans CPU and GPU compute, storage, energy and a 1.6T HIGH-SPEED SWITCH plus 'upcoming optical networking', sold with the Supermicro management software suite (SCM, SuperCloud Composer, SVM, SOM). The new 32-acre Silicon Valley DCBBS campus features an ADVANCED OPTICAL PHOTONICS NETWORKING LAB alongside datacenter-scale manufacturing, and management calls out high-speed switch and optical technology as areas of very aggressive continued investment, with the 'high bandwidth switch and the whole networking design management tool' cited as a big room to grow toward the ~20%-of-gross-profit DCBBS target. Customer networking readiness (alongside power and cooling) was one of the causes of the Q4 revenue push-out.
1.6T switch shipping in DCBBS; optical networking upcoming; SV photonics lab

CPO / ELSFP EXTERNAL LASER SOURCE ECONOMICS: ELSFP (external light source for co-packaged optics) is in very limited production now, ramping later in 2026 and through 2027 to ~400,000 PIECES PER MONTH IN 2028. Laser power scaling is the constraint: CPO/ELSFP uses a 300mW laser vs 70mW in an 800G transceiver and 100mW in a 1.6T transceiver, with die size ~6x larger, so meeting CPO demand requires the industry laser market to be 8-10x BIGGER than today; the next generation of ELSFP moves to DWDM, where yield loss is 40-50% worse than 1310nm. Laser capacity carries a 21-24 MONTH equipment-to-high-volume lead time. AOI is engaged with ~5 CPO customers on 3-4 year demand; several have already qualified AOI on fixed-wavelength CPO laser / ELSFP, with DWDM the current focus. High-volume ELSFP manufacturing is 'more like late Q3 next year' (late 2027). Houston laser fab capacity to grow ~300% by Q3 2027 plus a SECOND FAB cleanroom ~4x the size of the current facility (adding MOCVD, epi, steppers). Margin mix: laser gross margin 55-65%, ELSFP module ('EOSAP') >50%, both landing H2 2027. AOI is absent from first-generation CPO deployments purely because laser capacity must first feed AOI's own transceivers.
ELSFP ~400k pcs/month in 2028; 300mW CPO laser vs 70mW(800G)/100mW(1.6T); industry laser capacity needs 8-10x; laser GM 55-65%

US-MANUFACTURING POLICY TAILWIND: on reports of a potential US ban on Chinese-made optical transceivers, management says its US manufacturing presence is 'probably the most important element of our appeal to our customers' and that AOI is and expects to remain THE LARGEST DOMESTIC US MANUFACTURER of AI optical transceivers; three customers are in long-term-agreement discussions and early feedback is that customers will award AOI 'much more share' for US-manufactured product, though AOI cannot add incremental US capacity for it before Q3 2027. On Chinese laser competition: most Chinese suppliers are at 70mW with very few at 100mW, and management sees no credible 300mW DWDM CPO laser out of China for 'at least two, three years or even longer'.
Largest US domestic AI-transceiver manufacturer; 3 customers in long-term agreement talks; China 300mW CPO laser 2-3+ yrs away

Named by AOI management on its Q2 FY2026 call as one of the very few suppliers able to serve the high-power CPO laser market: AOI, Lumentum, Coherent and Broadcom are all 'invest[ing] huge money' in laser capacity, yet 'even combined... it's still very tough to meet the customer demand in the next few years'. Sizing: CPO/ELSFP needs a 300mW laser (vs 70mW for 800G, 100mW for 1.6T) with ~6x larger die, so the industry laser market must grow 8-10x; DWDM ELSFP carries 40-50% worse yield loss than 1310nm, and laser equipment takes 21-24 months from order to high-volume output. AOI states only AOI, Lumentum and Coherent can hit acceptable DWDM CPO laser / CPO module yields.
Industry high-power laser capacity must grow 8-10x for CPO; 21-24 month equipment lead time

THE NPO / SCALE-UP THESIS AND THE III-V ROADMAP: SiPho pluggables (800G/1.6T) have 'for the most part ALREADY REPLACED COPPER for scale-out connections outside the rack'; the NEXT FRONTIER IS SCALE-UP, where Tower has SEVERAL NEAR-PACKAGED-OPTICS (NPO) DEPLOYMENTS PLANNED OVER THE NEXT YEAR and many more in design — NPO expected to be 'in the TENS OF PERCENT' of SiPho shipments by H2 2027 (it reuses the pluggable ecosystem, easing hyperscaler reliability/serviceability/multi-source concerns). Content growth comes from HETEROGENEOUS INTEGRATION: III-V-on-silicon INTEGRATED InP LASERS (several tens of $M of revenue expected in 2027; chip-to-wafer bonding moving in-house), die-to-wafer/wafer-to-wafer bonding, and next-gen modulators (400G/lane silicon with Coherent; TFLN and InP in development); multi-year IQE EPI SUPPLY AGREEMENT resolved the InP-substrate crunch. SiGe: 100G/200G-per-lane drivers and TIAs in HVM across all three 200mm fabs (pluggables + LPO/LRO), 400G/lane next with tight EIC-PIC co-design. Adjacent read-through: image-sensor demand SURGING for machine-vision inspection driven by 'the accelerated build-out of DDR and HBM MEMORY ASSEMBLY LINES.'
NPO = tens-of-% of SiPho shipments by H2-2027; integrated InP lasers = tens of $M in 2027; pluggables already displaced copper for scale-out

DATA CENTER IS NOW ~50% OF NSE REVENUE - AND IT IS ALL OPTICAL. CEO Khaykin sized the segments for the first time this precisely: data center ~50% of NSE, aerospace & defense ~17%, the rest service provider. 'Pretty much when we talk about data center, it's all optical' - optical in R&D/lab, optical for PRODUCTION test, optical for fiber monitoring and build-out - 'there's very little copper or anything, if anything at all'. The data-center business MORE THAN DOUBLED YoY EXCLUDING SPIRENT, and the fastest-growing piece is production test: 'everything from making fiber optic modules to making fiber optic cables to now getting into the CPO testing, where we're entering the TRADITIONAL SEMICONDUCTOR TEST. We play the OPTICAL PLANE of the semiconductor test, and that's a completely new market.' Product proof point: Viavi launched 'the industry's first validation solution for ULTRA ETHERNET TRANSPORT, purpose-built to support large-scale AI and high-performance computing workloads' (ahead of schedule on the Spirent roadmap integration; Spirent synergies/restructuring complete as of the June quarter, and Spirent revenue is guided +~10% QoQ into September with December its strongest quarter). Capex read-through offered by the CEO: 'if you tell me somebody's spent this year $600 billion and next year they're going to spend $1 trillion, I should expect at least that kind of growth... on this particular product lines, we should do BETTER than the purely CapEx growth' because 1.6T brings insertions where Viavi is 'not even present' today. A&D growth is driven by PNT (positioning, navigation, timing), called a multi-year driver; service provider is up on fiber monitoring for build-outs and cable DAA migration, while wireless stays 'anemic, although stable'.
Data center ~50% of NSE (A&D ~17%); DC business >2x YoY ex-Spirent; first Ultra Ethernet Transport validation solution

SPEED-NODE, CPO AND OCS ROADMAP FROM THE TEST SEAT. SPEED MIX: '800 Gbps is still the biggest driver, but 1.6 Tbps is ramping very quickly, and that's mainly a lot of the production' - management expects 'probably in 2027 it may get to PARITY between 800 Gbps and 1.6 Tbps, and then 1.6 Tbps will continue to get bigger while 800 Gbps may pull back'; 400G 'is going to be around for quite a while as well. They just don't go away' - multiple nodes running in parallel. CPO: asked about yield-driven slippage, Khaykin was emphatic - 'there's been a lot of industry talk, like, oh, because the yield is going to be slower. That's all NONSENSE. CPO and all that thing is MOVING FORWARD... I have POs to show for that.' Viavi is already recognizing some CPO revenue in the September quarter with December 'starting to accelerate'. Crucially, yield management INCREASES test intensity: 'to manage yields, you just do more tests - more of a KNOWN GOOD DIE, KNOWN GOOD OPTICAL ENGINE, KNOWN GOOD SUBSTRATE... which means a lot of testing, which ultimately pretty good for us.' And the cleanest statement yet of why CPO happens at all: 'if you have co-packaged optics, your THREE NANOMETER SILICON PERFORMS AS A TWO NANOMETER SILICON. You are getting almost a WHOLE NODE OF ADVANTAGE by co-packaging the optics' - taken either as performance or as cost, at the price of complexity and yield. OCS: some revenue already in the numbers with 'the majority... coming in the next several quarters'; Viavi has been selling equipment to 'a big OCS vendor, hyperscaler, who makes their own stuff', and it is now broadening as 'many other companies are looking to do more optical switching in their core' - 'I see this demand as being very healthy.'
800G/1.6T parity ~2027 then 1.6T leads; CPO revenue starts Sept qtr, accelerates Dec; CPO = ~one node of silicon advantage

CALL — OPEN CPO STANCE AND THE SCALE-UP VIEW: scale-up philosophy = 'COPPER IF YOU CAN, OPTICS IF YOU MUST.' Arista rejects the ~5 proprietary CPO implementations circulating and is committing to ONE OPEN CPO — socketed optical engines, pigtail fibers, fully pre-tested modules, a truly open multi-vendor interface (often called NPO) — with trials/examples NEXT YEAR; 'the MAJORITY of the world will still remain PLUGGABLE OPTICS AND COPPER; there will be SOME co-packaged optics in 2028 and 2029.' Scale-up positioning: 'we live in an NVIDIA world' — where NVIDIA supplies the full NVLink vertical stack there is little Arista participation (Arista wins scale-out/across), but for NON-NVIDIA accelerators (AMD MI series, Google TPUs — 'increasingly a FORMIDABLE training processor', in-house XPUs, inference chips) Arista works BOTH scale-up and scale-out, including CUSTOM RACKS tuned to customers' engines; 'feels like InfiniBand 2-3 years ago... it will take time to move from proprietary NVLink to alternatives, even if Ethernet's really good — I expect us to do much better there.' 1.6T cadence (history repeats 800G's trials-2023/24 -> ramp-2025/26): TRIALS H2 2026 with single-digit VERY LARGE customers; REAL PRODUCTION 2027 (liquid-cooling infrastructure required). EOS innovations for AI fabrics: SSU hitless upgrades, MRC packet-spray/reassembly (kills hash-collision slowdowns), SRv6 explicit-path load balancing with real-time congestion signals — one binary from scale-out to scale-across.
Open CPO (socketed/NPO) trials 2027; majority stays pluggable+copper, some CPO 2028-29; non-NVIDIA scale-up = the opening (InfiniBand analogy); 1.6T production 2027

CALL — OPTICAL ROADMAP IN THREE PHASES (unlocks 'tens of billions of dollars' beyond the copper TAM): (1) high-density FIBER-ATTACHED solutions on aiXscale core tech (up to 50-meter fiber, ultra-low latency) — initial opportunity with a TIER-1 AI PLATFORM PROVIDER enters VOLUME PRODUCTION IN 2027; (2) NEAR-PACKAGED OPTICS (NPO) chipsets for multi-rack scale-up clusters, also 2027 production; (3) fully integrated Scorpio X switches with CPO optical-engine modules from 2028+, terabits/sec of optical I/O per switch. Management expects copper and optical to COEXIST: scale-up WITHIN a rack stays copper this generation and next, optical takes over as clusters span 4-5+ racks — and $/XPU content GOES UP moving copper->NPO. Full-stack capability (EIC + silicon photonics + aiXscale connector) enables complete optical engines, not just components.

Technology roadmap. Bigger reticle sizes drive panel/more-complex CoWoS first, then POWER DELIVERY becomes the next constraint over the following two to three years.
panel 310x310mm production Q1 2027; glass substrate not within 12 months; full-process ~USD 300M 2026; CPO launches late 2026

DEMAND DRIVERS AND CUSTOMERS: optical connectivity deployment in AI data centers is accelerating 'as hyperscalers scale GPU dense architectures and look for higher speed lower power photonics'. Near term the pull is the industry migration to 1.6T transceiver modules, 'for which indium phosphide based lasers and detectors are essential'; longer term, hyperscalers advancing toward NEAR-PACKAGED AND CO-PACKAGED OPTICS 'will continue to drive increasing demand for our material' — pointing to a durable multiyear demand cycle. AXT signed strategic LONG-TERM SUPPLY AGREEMENTS with COHERENT and another partner, and announced one with LUMENTUM the week of the call. US cloud/AI capex is the primary driver for EML and silicon-photonics transceivers plus high-speed photodetectors; AXT believes its material is used at MULTIPLE US HYPERSCALERS with end-customer use expected to broaden, alongside 'huge growth in China'. Corporate: subsidiary Tongmei withdrew its STAR Market IPO application (06-26-2026) and is redirecting to a HONG KONG EXCHANGE listing (~1 year); this created a redemption right on $49M of 2021 PE investment, though those investors currently wish to remain.
1.6T migration + CPO/NPO drive multiyear InP cycle; LTAs with Coherent and Lumentum; Tongmei to HKEX

RECORD REVENUE, GROSS PROFIT AND EPS, above the high end of the outlook: Q2 revenue $258.2M, +14.2% sequentially and +31.9% YoY, with HIGH BANDWIDTH MEMORY explicitly named (with co-packaged optics) as the key growth initiative driving the sequential increase in Probe Cards. GAAP gross margin 50.7%; GAAP EPS $0.71, non-GAAP EPS $0.82. The four-quarter arc CEO Mike Slessor cites: revenue +>30%, non-GAAP gross margin +1,500bps, EPS TRIPLED — 'years of investment to create and expand our unique position at the INTERSECTION OF HIGH-PERFORMANCE COMPUTE AND ADVANCED PACKAGING.' Q3 guided to ANOTHER RECORD: $270M +/- $10M with non-GAAP gross margin 54% +/- 1.5% and non-GAAP EPS $0.86 +/- $0.09, on strength in Foundry & Logic and Systems momentum.
Record $258.2M (+31.9% YoY); HBM + CPO named drivers; Q3 guide record $270M, non-GAAP GM 54%

CO-PACKAGED OPTICS TEST IS RUNNING AHEAD OF PLAN. FormFactor entered 2026 guiding $10-20M of CPO revenue, raised it to the high end a quarter ago, and now expects to EXCEED $20M BY THE END OF Q3 and to 'significantly exceed the $20 million level for the year overall'; systems-segment revenue nearly DOUBLED sequentially to a record $48.5M largely on this acceleration. Two drivers: growing CPO chip volumes planned for later this year, and leadership in 'the all-important TEST INSERTION ONE, which ensures KNOWN GOOD DIE on the PHOTONIC INTEGRATED CIRCUIT (PIC) wafer before it's combined with the electrical integrated circuit (EIC) to form the optical module in SCALE-UP AND SCALE-OUT network switches'. Management frames this as 'the very early stages of widespread adoption of silicon photonics in the broader semiconductor industry' as 'traditional copper interconnect is reaching physical limits in speed, heat and energy consumption', backed by a decade-long lab-to-fab first-mover advantage; served market sized at ~$400M by 2030. CPO revenue is recognized through the leading foundry (a 10% customer at 11% of Q2 revenue).
2026 CPO revenue to significantly exceed $20M (>$20M by end-Q3); ~$400M served market by 2030

RECORD REVENUE, GROSS PROFIT AND EPS, exceeding the high end of the outlook: Q2 (ended 06-27-2026) revenue $258.2M (+14.2% QoQ, +31.9% YoY); GAAP gross margin 50.7%; GAAP EPS $0.71 / non-GAAP $0.82 (versus $0.12 / $0.27 a year earlier). Broad-based demand with the two named growth initiatives — HIGH BANDWIDTH MEMORY (Probe Cards) and CO-PACKAGED OPTICS (Systems) — each driving sequential segment increases. Q3 guided to ANOTHER record: revenue $270M +/- $10M, non-GAAP gross margin 54% +/- 1.5%, non-GAAP EPS $0.86 +/- $0.09, with particular strength in FOUNDRY & LOGIC.
Record $258.2M, GAAP GM 50.7%, EPS tripled in 4 qtrs; Q3 record guide $270M / 54% GM

value: 11% of Q2 revenue (10% customer); Taiwan revenue +30% QoQ

CALL — THE ATE-TAM RERATING AND THE DUAL-VENDOR SHARE MACHINE: AI-driven revenue is now >60% OF TOTAL COMPANY REVENUE. New TAM frame: test equipment has rocketed from ~4% of semiconductor capex (2023) to 7% (2025) to 8% (first five months of 2026), expected to SETTLE AT 7-9%; with WFE approaching $250B by end of decade, Teradyne sees a path for TOTAL ATE TAM TO REACH OR EXCEED $20 BILLION — after a decade of semi-cap outgrowing test, THE TREND REVERSED IN 2024 and test now outpaces fab equipment (transistor production +15-20% CAGR = first-order SoC-TAM predictor; correlation runs on a ~1-YEAR LAG, strong over 3-5-year windows). Advanced packaging is the second engine: more chiplets/HBM/CPO per package raises test intensity per die. SHARE: first MERCHANT GPU order DELIVERED in Q2; CORRELATION COMPLETED AT A SECOND AI HYPERSCALER in Q3. Dual-vendor framework at big compute customers (supply de-risking): 4 phases over 9-12 months to first ramp, then a FAST-FOLLOWER phase taking share from 0% to ~30%; status — one compute customer at MATURE dual-vendor, one in FAST FOLLOWER, one IN QUALIFICATION; gains land GRADUALLY, socket-by-socket, from 2027 ('compute next surge H1-2027'). Vs Advantest: memory share shifting TO Teradyne (Advantest concurs), SoC roughly flat. Arm-share shift in server CPUs = additional Teradyne opportunity. Test intensity: accelerator:CPU ~4:1, but 'ALL the wafers that get fabbed need to get tested' — mix-agnostic at the wafer level. 2027: 'a RESURGENCE in growth' on TAM expansion + share; target-model update at the Q4 call. Networking test: CPO test TAM $300-700M BY 2028 (2027 nearer ~$200M), Photon 100 + Quantifi + MLTP JV cover pluggable->XPO->CPO and copper; SiPho nuance — the polymer LENS is applied after EIC-PIC bonding, so key loss/polarization tests CANNOT happen at insertion 1.
Test = 8% of semi capex (was 4% in '23), settling 7-9%; ATE TAM path >=$20B; 2nd hyperscaler correlation DONE; dual-vendor: 0->30% fast-follower share; 2027 resurgence

CALL — PHOTONICS: A $10B MAP BY 2030, AND THE LTA MODEL: Corning's new PHOTONICS Market-Access Platform targets $10 BILLION of revenue by 2030 — passive photonics INSIDE THE BOX (FAU harnesses and everything that moves/manages light between the faceplate and the silicon-photonics optical engine) for CPO/NPO, where Corning historically had ZERO content; likely starts with scale-out, and optical SCALE-UP supercharges it; the plan is built on 'assumptions and discussions AND AGREEMENTS with customers.' Despite industry chatter on scale-up timing, 'NO CHANGES to our fundamental belief... inside the real ecosystem there is much less drama than what it looks like from outside.' Business model: long-term agreements (Amazon multi-billion, NVIDIA, Meta up-to-$6B, Apple) will be 'the LION'S SHARE of our optical business' — every major capacity expansion is underpinned by risk/reward-sharing LTAs; profitability comes from innovation value-share, not bare-fiber pricing (optical NI +77% to a record 21% margin). Springboard math: run rate $20B by end-2026 (Q3 guide may hit it a QUARTER EARLY) -> $30B (2028) -> $40B (2030), 19% CAGR; high-confidence variant $27B/$35B; biggest risk-adjustment between the two = SCALE-UP TIMING. Elsewhere: memory prices push handsets down mid-teens % (Gorilla outperforms on content) but push TVs LARGER/premium (favors Gen 10.5); solar recovers from Q3 toward a $3B stream, with MORE POLYSILICON SHIFTING TO SEMICONDUCTOR (ELECTRONIC) GRADE at Hemlock; FY capex ~$2B.
Photonics MAP = $10B by 2030 (inside-the-box passive, zero prior content); LTAs = lion's share of optical; $20B run rate possibly a qtr early

Introduced the Ethernet E835 portfolio scaling 10GbE to 200GbE across cloud/AI/enterprise/edge/telco. Physical AI: >130 customers adopting or testing Core Ultra Series 3 / Core Series 3 for edge AI and robotics, plus OpenVINO Physical AI framework. Strategic collaborations announced with Foxconn, Siemens, Hitachi, Echo Neurotechnologies and Greenstone Biosciences to co-develop industry-specific AI and compute solutions on Intel processors and purpose-built silicon.
Xeon 6+ = first server product on 18A; Xeon+SambaNova+Blackwell agentic rack-scale

CALL — SERVER DEMAND AND THE CPU:GPU RATIO: Q2 beat the guidance midpoint by $1.8 BILLION (7th straight beat); AI-driven businesses grew >70% YoY and are now ~70% OF REVENUE (from 60% in Q1). Q2 YoY server growth was the STRONGEST ON RECORD; DCAI operating margin hit 40% ($2.5B, +$1B QoQ). Intel is UNDERSHIPPING demand by >$1B/quarter and 'will NOT catch up' even in Q4 — supply growth is skewed to end-Q3/Q4, especially servers; GRANITE RAPIDS IS 'EXTREMELY TIGHT' (Intel 3 the critical node). Choke points beyond wafers: advanced packaging, SUBSTRATES, T-GLASS and MEMORY — 'probably our most challenged parts of the supply chain.' Industry server-CPU units to grow strong double digits THIS YEAR AND NEXT with momentum into 2028; pricing is ASP-PER-CORE so rising core counts lift ASPs → DCAI revenue CAGR 'well NORTH of double digits' for the next few years. On the CPU:GPU ratio: 'we're almost in PARITY at this point and could eventually even skew MORE TO CPUs on a unit basis.' On AMD's new $220B-by-2030 server TAM: no number offered, but the market 'is going to grow significantly.' PC side: market down low-double-digits in 2026 on memory costs — Intel will PIVOT as much wafer production as possible to data-center CPUs; client strength was largely ASP (mix + like-for-like price increases passing on inflation); AI PC now two-thirds of client mix; edge ~10% of CCPG.
Beat by $1.8B; record server growth; DCAI margin 40%; undershipping >$1B/qtr into Q4; CPU:GPU ~parity -> CPU skew; DCAI CAGR well north of DD

CALL — ASIC/PURPOSE-BUILT AND MEMORY STRATEGY: purpose-built silicon (design services/ASIC) revenue grew ~20% QoQ and nearly TRIPLED YoY; run rate 'approaching $2 BILLION' -> '$4 BILLION run rate in the not too distant future' against a $100B+ TAM — anchored by CPU/XPU design capability, the IP portfolio, advanced packaging (EMIB-T) and leading-edge process; Fortinet next-gen security processor win; IPUs already supplied to hyperscalers; roadmap from networking to compute to eventually ACCELERATORS. MEMORY: Intel hired SEOK-HEE LEE, former CEO of SK HYNIX; memory is 'the big supply-constraint challenge' — collaborating with all three big memory vendors — and Intel is exploring COMPUTE-MEMORY INTEGRATION, stacking, and better memory utilization ('stay tuned'; analyst cited Intel 'Z-Angle Memory' / 'Cross-Batch Memory' development work). Also announced a Google Cloud collaboration to run Intel's operations AI-first, and customer PREPAYS are already unlocking capacity.
ASIC run rate ~$2B -> $4B target ($100B+ TAM, ~3x YoY); ex-SK Hynix CEO Seok-Hee Lee hired; compute+memory integration explored

Intel Foundry revenue $5.8B, UP 31% YoY (segment revenue including intersegment). Node progress: INTEL 18A-P ENTERED RISK PRODUCTION, meeting the timeline shared with customers a year earlier while adding performance, power and thermal-resistance improvements to the 18A platform; Intel launched Xeon 6+ as its first server-class product on Intel 18A. Intel Foundry ENTERED HIGH-VOLUME MANUFACTURING for a subset of Core Ultra Series 3 (Panther Lake) using ASML's EXE HIGH-NA EUV — the first HVM use of High-NA in the chain. Company-wide beat driven partly by 'volume upside driven by HIGHER FACTORY YIELDS and improved cycle times' (CFO), with investment 'meaningfully increasing' in equipment, clean-room space and substrates.
Foundry rev $5.8B (+31% YoY); 18A-P risk production; High-NA EUV in HVM (Panther Lake)

Intel Foundry revenue $5.8B, UP 31% YoY. INTEL 18A-P ENTERED RISK PRODUCTION on the timeline shared with customers and partners a year earlier, extending the 18A platform with enhanced performance, power and thermal resistance; Xeon 6+ launched as Intel's first server-class product on Intel 18A. Intel Foundry ENTERED HIGH-VOLUME MANUFACTURING for a subset of Core Ultra Series 3 (Panther Lake) using ASML's EXE HIGH-NA EUV. Purpose-built silicon expanded beyond networking/IPUs via a strategic collaboration with FORTINET to build the Fortinet Security Processor 6 using Intel's advanced design, PACKAGING and manufacturing. Capacity: €5B investment announced to expand manufacturing and increase production of Xeon 6 and next-generation Xeon on INTEL 3; Bowers campus expanded to grow Intel Mask Operations capability for leading-edge process development. Seok-Hee Lee appointed to lead ADVANCED PACKAGING. CEO frames the opportunity as 'CPU franchise, ASICs, ADVANCED PACKAGING and vast wafer foundry network'.
Foundry $5.8B (+31% YoY); 18A-P risk production; High-NA EUV HVM; Fortinet SP6; EUR5B on Intel 3

Advanced packaging elevated organizationally and commercially: Seok-Hee Lee appointed to LEAD ADVANCED PACKAGING, and CEO Lip-Bu Tan names 'advanced packaging' as one of four pillars ('CPU franchise, ASICs, advanced packaging and vast wafer foundry network'). New packaging-inclusive external win: strategic collaboration with FORTINET to develop the Fortinet Security Processor 6 using Intel's advanced design, PACKAGING and manufacturing capabilities — extending purpose-built silicon beyond networking and IPUs. Intel Foundry revenue $5.8B (+31% YoY); company 'meaningfully increasing' investment in equipment, clean-room space and SUBSTRATES to support product and foundry growth this year and next.
Dedicated adv-packaging leader named; Fortinet SP6 packaging win; substrate investment up

CALL — CAPEX RAISED AGAIN, AND THE INFRA STACK: Q2 CAPEX WAS $44.9 BILLION (~60% servers / ~40% data centers + networking; H1 = $80.6B with Q1's $35.7B), driving NEGATIVE free cash flow of $5.9B in the quarter (OCF $39.1B). FULL-YEAR 2026 CAPEX GUIDANCE RAISED TO $195-205 BILLION (from $180-190B) on 'an acceleration in the delivery of capacity to meet growing demand'; 2027 capex to INCREASE SIGNIFICANTLY again. Funding: debt portfolio expanded from ~$16B to ~$100B in 12 months + the June $49.6B equity raise; no further equity planned (ATM only for SBC tax); cash + securities $242.5B. Infrastructure differentiators: VIRGO NETWORK connects up to A MILLION AI ACCELERATORS across multiple data-center sites into one unified supercomputer; software stack natively supports JAX/PyTorch/vLLM/SGLang for GPU<->TPU portability; new AGENT-OPTIMIZED AXION CPU delivers 30% better performance/dollar than peers; accelerator portfolio spans TPU 8t/8i and the new NVIDIA VERA RUBIN platform. TPU ALLOCATION PRIORITIES: (1) frontier AGI development ('the foundation for everything'), (2) core products (Search/YouTube) and serving first-party models for Cloud (Vertex/Gemini Enterprise), (3) external infrastructure demand — balanced by placing TPUs in customers' or partners' data centers.
Q2 capex $44.9B (FCF -$5.9B); FY26 guide RAISED to $195-205B; Virgo net = 1M accelerators unified; Axion +30% perf/$

AGENTIC AI SHIFTS THE CPU/ACCELERATOR MIX: CEO C.C. Wei says 'the emergence of AGENTIC AI is leading to a RESURGENCE IN THE ROLE OF CPUs in AI data centers, which drive more silicon demand IN ADDITION TO AI accelerators.' TSMC calls this a positive because 'no matter what CPU approach is taken, whether it's x86, Arm-based, or RISC-V architecture, they are almost all TSMC's customers' — and TSMC is working with customers to ALLOCATE WAFER SUPPLY to balance the CPU / GPU / XPU ratio. AI-related demand described as 'extremely robust' with cloud-service-provider customers and their customers providing 'very strong signal and positive outlook', keeping conviction in the multi-year AI megatrend 'very high'. Counterpoint flagged: consumer and price-sensitive end-market segments 'are being challenged due to the impact of RISING COMPONENT PRICES and macroeconomic uncertainties', so TSMC is being prudent in business planning.
Agentic AI = CPU resurgence (x86/Arm/RISC-V all TSMC); wafer allocated across CPU/GPU/XPU

Foundry backdrop for the Rubin generation: Q2 revenue $40.2B with HPC UP 20% SEQUENTIALLY to 66% of total revenue; 2nm reached 3% of wafer revenue in its first meaningful quarter and is in a STEEP RAMP that will dilute gross margin 3-4 points in H2; Q3 guided to $44.6-45.8B (+37% YoY). FY2026 revenue growth raised to slightly above 40%, and the capital budget raised to $60-64B. AI demand 'extremely robust' with CSPs and their customers giving 'very strong signal and positive outlook'. NEW MIX DYNAMIC: agentic AI is driving a RESURGENCE OF CPUs in AI data centers 'in addition to AI accelerators' — TSMC is allocating wafer supply to balance the CPU/GPU/XPU ratio, and notes x86, Arm-based and RISC-V CPU vendors are almost all TSMC customers. Constraint to watch for accelerator output: advanced PACKAGING capacity 'so tight that now it's limiting my customers' growth'.
HPC 66% of revenue (+20% QoQ); 2nm at 3% and ramping steeply; packaging tightness limits customers

OPTICAL IS NOW AEHR'S SECOND PILLAR: optical device test and burn-in for DATA CENTER INFRASTRUCTURE TRANSCEIVERS, CHIP-TO-CHIP I/O and hard disk drives accounted for approximately 20% OF FISCAL 2026 REVENUE, alongside AI accelerators/CPUs/network processors at ~71% — and management expects BOTH markets to grow significantly in fiscal 2027. Silicon photonics is named as one of the two focus areas (with AI accelerators) that together drove the majority of fourth-quarter revenue. Company-wide: record quarterly bookings, record effective backlog over $100M, and FY2027 revenue guided to $130-150M (2.6x-3x fiscal 2026) with 18-22% non-GAAP pretax margin and no capacity constraint at that level. Two years ago over 95% of Aehr's revenue was EV silicon carbide; today almost 95% comes from other markets.
Optical/data-centre device burn-in ~20% of FY26 revenue; silicon photonics a named growth driver

END-MARKET TRANSFORMATION COMPLETE — from EV silicon carbide to AI: two years ago OVER 95% of Aehr's business was tied to silicon carbide for electric vehicles; in fiscal 2026 almost 95% of revenue came from markets OTHER than EV SiC. Reliability and production WAFER-LEVEL BURN-IN and screening for AI ACCELERATORS, CPUs AND NETWORK PROCESSORS were the fastest-growing markets and accounted for approximately 71% OF TOTAL ANNUAL REVENUE; OPTICAL DEVICE TEST AND BURN-IN for data-center transceivers, chip-to-chip I/O and hard disk drives added another 20%. Q4 exceeded consensus with RECORD QUARTERLY BOOKINGS and a record backlog (effective backlog over $100 million). FY2027 GUIDANCE: revenue $130-150 MILLION, representing 2.6x to 3x fiscal 2026 revenue, with non-GAAP pretax profitability of 18-22%; management says it is NOT CAPACITY LIMITED even at the $150M level and sees scope to raise guidance further as additional orders materialise.
FY27 guide $130-150M (2.6-3x FY26); AI processors ~71% of revenue, optical ~20%; backlog >$100M

NEW AI DESIGN-IN PIPELINE: Aehr completed benchmark testing of its wafer-level burn-in solution on a processor from 'a major supplier of AI accelerators, CPUs, and network processors', with results that exceeded the customer's expectations and, in the customer's words, were 'better than they can get at the package level'. That top-tier AI processor supplier now wants to move to PILOT PRODUCTION TEST VALIDATION AT ITS SEMICONDUCTOR CONTRACT MANUFACTURER IN TAIWAN — and, notably, wants to pull in its CURRENT high-volume device rather than waiting for the next-generation device the benchmark was originally scoped for. Separately, additional AI-processor customers are evaluating wafer-level burn-in to improve reliability and reduce yield loss from later-stage production burn-in, including one of Aehr's largest PACKAGE-level burn-in customers now asking about a wafer-level evaluation for a future AI accelerator and CPU, in parallel with its Sonoma package-level needs. (Aehr does not name any of these customers.)
Benchmark 'better than package level'; top-tier AI supplier moving to pilot production in Taiwan

Sequential revenue +15% reflects higher server ASPs from DRAM/NAND inflationary costs; networking products constrained by DDR4/DDR5 and wafer capacity ('supply chain is the name of the game in networking' — purchase commitments +40% sequentially). FY2026 guide assumes NO incremental supply; component costs expected elevated into 2027 until new fabs yield. Inferencing accelerating as a demand driver — 'a lot of these inferencing deployments will be done on CPUs', traditional-server orders up triple digits on agentic-AI/high-memory configs; by end of decade Neri expects MOST demand to be inferencing. FY2027 framework: revenue +8-12% with AI-systems revenue accelerating.
DRAM/NAND-driven ASPs; no incremental 2026 supply; FY27 +8-12%
RTX Spark N1X chip includes a custom 20-core Grace CPU built in partnership with MediaTek, fused with Blackwell RTX GPU via NVLink, on TSMC 3nm, with 70 billion transistors and 128GB unified memory.
70 billion transistors; 128GB unified memory; 1 petaflop AI performance
→ NVIDIA: A custom 20-core Grace CPU built in partnership with MediaTek, fused by NVLink into the RTX Spark N1X chip.

Agentic AI is expanding the CPU TAM: 'the agent needs support of a CPU... the harness — the CPU runs it, makes the calls, manages memory, and is in the loop in every decision an agent makes' (all 3 microprocessor leaders cited CPU TAM expansion). Traditional server revenue +92% with absolute unit growth AND content growth. Architecture mix: large direct-liquid-cooled GPU deployments (GB200/B300, Vera) are biased to Arm, while enterprise B200/B300/RTX 6000 Pro systems are x86; traditional servers remain x86 today, with Vera CPU seen as future relief for the microprocessor shortage.
Traditional servers +92%; big GPU racks Arm-biased, enterprise x86

Supply-constraint rank order per Jeff Clarke: DRAM, NAND, CPUs (microprocessors), then hard drives, then 'the basket of goods around that'. Trailing semiconductor nodes are filling at greater rates, leading-edge nodes fully allocated with ~1-year lead times. Dell is 'repricing every day' in the inflationary environment, and customers are signing 3-5 year multiyear supply agreements to secure access. Year-over-year, each server carries MORE cores, MORE DRAM and MORE NAND (content growth on top of unit growth).
Constraint order: DRAM > NAND > CPU > HDD; leading-edge lead times ~1 year

Pipeline & TAM: NRE pipeline "very, very strong", especially North America - accelerator, CPU and networking ASIC projects on hyperscaler capex; AI designs migrating N5/N3 -> N3/N2; multiple ASIC design opportunities from NA hyperscalers (in progress to win another hyperscaler; currently ONE major hyperscaler account). Networking: multiple NA data-center networking customers - ONE approaching production, another with N3 in design and N2 kicking off soon; each "meaningful" project = >$100M annual revenue in coming years. Accelerator startups: their N3 production revenue most likely H1 2027; their N2 ~2028. Automotive: volume production started, ramps Q2, #1 revenue contributor in H1 2026 / #2 for the full year; next-gen auto chip tape-out by Q3 2026; industry trend to 2-4 chips per vehicle; targeting 1-2 more China automakers (robotics applications too). TAM view: ~$100B AI-ASIC TAM next year called "pretty accurate"; TSMC raised its 2030 overall TAM to $1.5T at the US symposium; Google+Amazon still >90% of ASIC revenue. De-risking: majority of design resources now OUTSIDE China (Japan office up to 250 staff, Malaysia+Vietnam >120 engineers); new Chief Business Officer hired from NVIDIA (ex-Xilinx, data-center/hyperscaler background).
AI-ASIC TAM ~$100B 2027; networking projects >$100M/yr each; auto #1 in H1

Agentic AI driving demand multiplier: single user request routes to multiple AI models many times (vs once for traditional inference) → dramatically increases data traffic and latency requirements across the cluster; also drives more CPU deployment → more NICs, PCIe switches, retimers; Marvell sees Agentic AI as additional tailwind for interconnect, switching, and XPU attach

Acquiring Empower Semiconductor for integrated voltage regulator (IVR) + silicon-capacitor IP — the 'final piece' of ADI's grid-to-core vertical power-delivery platform at the XPU/GPU/CPU: shrinks customer power footprint up to 4x, cuts data-center compute power consumption an estimated 10-15%, and delivers the ultrafast transient response volatile AI workloads need. 'The biggest bottleneck AI is creating for us today is power density and delivery efficiency.' Small revenue at close; design-ins in train with significant revenue expected 2027.
Empower acq: power footprint -4x, DC power consumption -10-15%; revenue surge 2027

Four AI pillars: (1) AI infrastructure scaling — clusters integrating GPUs/CPUs/DPUs/switches/NICs/memory fabrics across vendors (Ethernet, UALink, PCIe, NVMe) incl. rack-backplane characterization for next-gen scale-up networks; (2) SPEED TRANSITIONS — 800G deployments accelerating 1.6T adoption with rising 3.2T R&D; (3) optical/photonics technologies; (4) system-level emulation. At OFC Keysight demonstrated 1.6T physical-layer solutions with 20+ industry leaders (traffic emulation, link reliability, SerDes signal integrity) and ran the industry's FIRST public Ultra Ethernet Consortium interoperability demo WITH BROADCOM.
1.6T test w/ 20+ leaders at OFC; first UEC interop demo w/ Broadcom; 3.2T R&D rising

Q1 2026 (DART quarterly report, consolidated): revenue KRW 20.6B (+35% YoY vs KRW 15.2B) with an operating LOSS of KRW 3.9B — narrowed from a KRW 6.4B loss a year earlier; FY2025 was loss-making (rev KRW 68.5B, OP -16.7B) on the design-services down-cycle. Samsung Foundry DSP + Arm Approved Design Partner; designing 2nm GAA BIG-DIE AI accelerators for datacenter/HPC plus edge generative-AI chips, with 2.5D/3D advanced-packaging mass-production support.

Product/strategy: HBM TC bonders (12/16-high stacking) remain the core. KEY DISCLOSURE: because the industry's HYBRID-BONDER development is DELAYED by technical hurdles, 20-high+ HBM stacking needs a new tool that can bond WIDER dies — Hanmi is about to launch the "WIDE TC BONDER" for next-gen HBM structures, while ALSO developing hybrid bonders (for HBM and for system-semiconductor stacking) in parallel. Portfolio extensions: 6-SIDE INSPECTION (pre/post-TC-bond HBM yield control), world-first two-in-one BOC+COB bonder (stacked GDDR, enterprise eSSD), entry into 2.5D PACKAGING (TC/FC/die bonders for interposer integration of HBM + base die + CPU/GPU), MSVP 8.0 saw/vision placement (world #1 since mid-2000s, boosted by larger PLP/chiplet panels), EMI Shield 2.0 X (#1 share). Disclosed customer list: SK Hynix, MICRON, ASE, Amkor, JCET, Huatian, TFME, Infineon, STMicro, PTI, Skyworks, Luxshare + Korean OSATs/Samsung Electro-Mechanics/LG Innotek.
WIDE TC bonder launch imminent (hybrid-bonder delay = TC extension); 2.5D packaging entry; Micron now a disclosed customer

Platform expansion: 2025-Q2 acquisitions of iSemi and Tech Dream added back-end TEST EQUIPMENT and CHEMICALS — module testers for AI accelerator/CPU + SOCAMM/LPCAMM/DRAM compatibility, high-speed burn-in testers, EFEM automation, and cleaning chemicals for post-etch DRAM/HBM — an explicit AI·HBM test-platform strategy on top of sockets.
iSemi/Tech Dream deals: SOCAMM module testers + HBM/DRAM cleaning chemicals

Industry-wide shortages 'across the board — wafers, silicon chips, CPUs, optics, and memory' now seen as a 1-2 YEAR phenomenon, not 1-2 quarters; chip lead times running 52 weeks reliably with reservation needs beyond that. Purchase commitments rose to $8.9B (from $6.8B in Q4), multiyear, mostly chips for new products and AI deployments. Deferred revenue $6.2B (from $5.37B) as AI qualification/acceptance cycles stretched from 2-4 quarters to 6-8 quarters (GPU rack-and-stack + manual cabling takes months). Arista will accept gross-margin pressure to assure supply: 'we do not want to keep GPUs idle because Arista did not supply the network'.
52-week lead times; purchase commitments $8.9B; quals now 6-8 quarters

Strong Q1 2026 enterprise results across data center and campus; #1 in >10GbE high-speed switching. Demand described as the best in the CEO's Arista tenure, but facing industry-wide component shortages — wafers, silicon chips, CPUs, optics, and especially memory — with elevated procurement costs; signing multiyear supply agreements and purchase commitments ($8.9B). Demand is outstripping supply in 2026, with expected gross-margin pressure from paying up to assure supply continuity.
industry-wide component shortages; $8.9B purchase commitments; GM pressure

Back-end AI fabric deployments now pull roughly 1:1 front-end network spend (wide-area, CPU, and storage networks; previously framed as 2:1). Diverse accelerators are broadening the opportunity: AMD MI-series XPU scale-out at a Neo Cloud (white-box-to-'Blue Box' conversion at 800G, thousands of XPUs) and TPU-architecture attach in scale-across multi-tenant use cases. Enterprise agentic-AI/inference clusters are emerging in the low thousands of accelerators ('the calm before the storm', reviving HPC-style high-performance compute).
Back-end:front-end now ~1:1; AMD XPU + TPU attach

Communications +33% QoQ on power solutions for optical modules and switches; storage strong (DDR5, HDD/SSD) pulled by data center; sampled first high-speed DDR5 interface products at major customers; CPU a continued tailwind; robotics / physical AI emerging

Package Solution (FCBGA/BGA substrates) revenue KRW 725.0B (+45% YoY) on AI/server demand — high-multilayer, large-area, embedded substrates for AI accelerators and server CPUs; began full-scale supply of AI data-center networking substrates to a new big-tech customer; BGA substrates for Arm processors and memory

Package Solution: FCBGA revenue up across all applications led by AI/servers — started FULL-SCALE supply of AI datacenter NETWORKING substrates to a NEW big-tech customer; focus on next-generation high-multilayer, large-area, EMBEDDED FCBGA for AI accelerators and server CPUs; BGA grew on substrates for ARM processors and memory, with increased high-end supply to global big-tech customers. Capacitors: revenue KRW 1,408.5B (+16% YoY, +7% QoQ) with strong AI-related growth across server, power and network equipment; high-end AI-server MLCC demand to stay strong.
AI networking substrates: full-scale supply to new big-tech customer

MonTitan enterprise controllers: end-user qualifications progressed so well that volume commercial ramp was pulled in ONE QUARTER EARLY (to current quarter); customers plan ramps at 3 Tier-1 ASIAN CSPs + 2 US Tier-1 CSPs later this year, with TLC-based CMX compute / KV-cache SSDs (near-CPU/near-GPU) first and QLC high-capacity AI storage later as 2-terabit QLC die broadens. MonTitan targeted at 5-10% of (raised) 2026 revenue. Next phase: first 4-nanometer controller — a PCIe Gen6 MonTitan for hyperscalers/CSPs — tapes out in Q3 2026 with Tier-1 design wins already secured, volume ramping meaningfully in 2028.
MonTitan ramp 1 qtr early; 3 Asian + 2 US Tier-1 CSPs; PCIe6 4nm tape-out Q3

Boot-drive/AI-infrastructure footprint expanding: Q4-2025 began volume boot-drive shipments to 'a leading AI GPU manufacturer' for its DPU; in Q1 qualified the next-generation DPU plus Ethernet and NVLINK switches of that customer's new GPU/CPU platform launching H2 2026 — footprint widens beyond the DPU with 2-4x density per device; also sampling with 'a leading search-engine company' for its TPU architecture. NAND sourcing is a moat: 2026 supply allocations were finalized by flash makers by MID-2025, and Silicon Motion secures NAND from 3 different makers; NAND vendors are retreating from edge/client segments (PC units now seen -10%+ in 2026, smartphones -10%+) to prioritize enterprise/cloud AI — accelerating controller outsourcing share gains.
NVLink-switch/DPU boot drives (H2 2026 platform); 2026 NAND allocations locked mid-2025
Named as Intel partner for heterogeneous AI inference (dataflow RDU architecture combined with Xeon 6)
→ Intel: Multiyear collaboration with Intel to design a next-generation heterogeneous AI inference architecture combining SambaNova RDUs and Intel Xeon 6 processors

DESIGN IP — the custom-silicon tell. Won MORE THAN 95% of PCIe 7.0 opportunities (up from >90% in Q2), including a subsystem win at a marquee enterprise storage customer. DIE-TO-DIE business ON PACE TO DOUBLE YEAR-OVER-YEAR with 100+ cumulative design wins. LPDDR6: 25 design wins year to date, silicon proven across multiple nodes and foundries. PCIe 7.0 >95% win rate; die-to-die 2x YoY, 100+ wins; LPDDR6 25 wins YTD; USB IP $2B lifetime bookings

→ Samsung: Samsung Foundry named among the customers that validated Multiphysics Fusion (up to 10x faster design closure, 3x faster runtime). SPEED-NODE, CPO AND OCS ROADMAP FROM THE TEST SEAT. SPEED MIX: '800 Gbps is still the biggest driver, but 1.6 Tbps is ramping very quickly, and that's mainly a lot of the production' - management expects 'probably in 2027 it may get to PARITY between 800 Gbps and 1.6 Tbps, and then 1.6 Tbps will continue to get bigger while 800 Gbps may pull back'; 400G 'is going to be around for quite a while as well. They just don't go away' - multiple nodes running in parallel. CPO: asked about yield-driven slippage, Khaykin was emphatic - 'there's been a lot of industry talk, like, oh, because the yield is going to be slower. That's all NONSENSE. CPO and all that thing is MOVING FORWARD... I have POs to show for that.' Viavi is already recognizing some CPO revenue in the September quarter with December 'starting to accelerate'. Crucially, yield management INCREASES test intensity: 'to manage yields, you just do more tests - more of a KNOWN GOOD DIE, KNOWN GOOD OPTICAL ENGINE, KNOWN GOOD SUBSTRATE... which means a lot of testing, which ultimately pretty good for us.' And the cleanest statement yet of why CPO happens at all: 'if you have co-packaged optics, your THREE NANOMETER SILICON PERFORMS AS A TWO NANOMETER SILICON. You are getting almost a WHOLE NODE OF ADVANTAGE by co-packaging the optics' - taken either as performance or as cost, at the price of complexity and yield. OCS: some revenue already in the numbers with 'the majority... coming in the next several quarters'; Viavi has been selling equipment to 'a big OCS vendor, hyperscaler, who makes their own stuff', and it is now broadening as 'many other companies are looking to do more optical switching in their core' - 'I see this demand as being very healthy.'

Data center revenue $107.7M, +140.4% Y/Y and +32.3% Q/Q. ~$471M/month DC transceiver revenue by mid-2027 (800G $217M + 1.6T $164M + 100/400G $90M); Q4 2026 >$500M

CAPACITY RAMP: 800G/1.6T manufacturing capacity is 'approaching 200,000 units per month' now, up from ~100,000/month exiting Q1 FY2026; expected to reach OVER 650,000 pieces/month by END-2026 and OVER 930,000 pieces/month by END-2027, with MORE THAN HALF of that output from TEXAS. The 210k sq ft facility (dedicated 800G/1.6T) starts initial production LATE in Q3; moving transceiver lines out of headquarters frees that fab to expand INDIUM PHOSPHIDE wafer capacity; Pearland (construction started) and Houston buildouts come online EARLY 2027. ~200k units/mo now -> >650k/mo end-2026 -> >930k/mo end-2027 (>50% from Texas); TX footprint >1.6M sqft; booked through Q2 2027

CPO / ELSFP EXTERNAL LASER SOURCE ECONOMICS: ELSFP (external light source for co-packaged optics) is in very limited production now, ramping later in 2026 and through 2027 to ~400,000 PIECES PER MONTH IN 2028. Laser power scaling is the constraint: CPO/ELSFP uses a 300mW laser vs 70mW in an 800G transceiver and 100mW in a 1.6T transceiver, with die size ~6x larger, so meeting CPO demand requires the industry laser market to be 8-10x BIGGER than today; the next generation of ELSFP moves to DWDM, where yield loss is 40-50% worse than 1310nm. Laser capacity carries a 21-24 MONTH equipment-to-high-volume lead time. AOI is engaged with ~5 CPO customers on 3-4 year demand; several have already qualified AOI on fixed-wavelength CPO laser / ELSFP, with DWDM the current focus. High-volume ELSFP manufacturing is 'more like late Q3 next year' (late 2027). Houston laser fab capacity to grow ~300% by Q3 2027 plus a SECOND FAB cleanroom ~4x the size of the current facility (adding MOCVD, epi, steppers). Margin mix: laser gross margin 55-65%, ELSFP module ('EOSAP') >50%, both landing H2 2027. AOI is absent from first-generation CPO deployments purely because laser capacity must first feed AOI's own transceivers.

BOTTLENECK HAS MOVED FROM LASERS TO DSP/TIA: because AOI makes its own lasers in-house it avoids the laser shortage that management calls 'the biggest bottleneck right now for the transceiver business' and 'the number one issue' for competitors; AOI's binding constraints for 800G/1.6T are instead DSP and TIA supply, where 'the whole supply chain is very tight' for 1.6T - AOI says its supplier ranks it FOURTH priority under a long-term partnership, with calls once or twice a week. Industry high-power laser capacity must grow 8-10x for CPO; 21-24 month equipment lead time

→ Coherent: Joint OFC announcement with Coherent of a 400G-PER-LANE MODULATOR IN SILICON — the next-generation figure-of-merit work (alongside Tower's thin-film lithium-niobate and InP modulator development) that anchors multi-generation exclusivity-style engagements.

CALL — THE FIBER-CONTENT-PER-GPU FRAMEWORK (the definitive supply-side math for optical in AI factories). Base case: enterprise grows at the rate GPUs grow; THREE drivers add on top. (1) CLUSTER SIZE: clusters ABOVE ~130,000 GPUs exceed a 512-radix switch's two-layer span and need a THIRD OPTICAL LAYER -> ~50% MORE CONTENT PER GPU for very large clusters. (2) BANDWIDTH (doubles ~every 2 years): Hopper -> Blackwell kept 100G SerDes so fibers went 8 -> 16 per GPU (content DOUBLED); the RUBIN era jumps SerDes to 200G with lane count flat -> NEUTRAL; Feynman (~2029-30): fibers double again IF SerDes stays 200G, neutral if 400G arrives (BiDi/WDM could offset) — Springboard conservatively assumes NEUTRAL. (3) SCALE-UP, today 100% COPPER: Vera Rubin Ultra NVL576 is a HYBRID step — copper inside each 72-GPU rack, DIRECT OPTICAL rack-to-rack. Bracketing a full-optical scale-up: 14.4 Tbps scale-up / 200G = 72 lanes x 2 fibers = 144, plus scale-out 1.6 Tbps / 200G = 16 fibers -> 160 FIBERS PER GPU = 10x today's 16-fiber scale-out-only content (reality lands between; % of optical ports is confidential). COMBINED: optical content per GPU +1.3-1.5x BY 2028 and 'much, much higher' toward 2030. Status: Q2 enterprise strength is 'ALL JUST SCALE-OUT — we are not yet seeing scale-up or photonics in our results'; orders accelerating; 'if we could make more, we could sell more.'
Content/GPU drivers: 3rd optical layer >130k GPUs (+50%); Blackwell 16 fibers; full-optical scale-up = 160 fibers/GPU (10x); +1.3-1.5x by 2028

POWER franchise detail: customers are pushing for greater than 98% conversion efficiency, multi-kilowatt delivery with peak power up to 2x rated load, plus protection, telemetry and fault recording. Significant design uptick for ADI protection and 800V-to-intermediate conversion technology delivering 20 kW at industry-leading power density exceeding 2.5 kW per cubic inch, as the industry transitions to 800V DC power distribution. At the intermediate-to-core conversion layer - called ONE OF THE FASTEST AND LARGEST GROWING ANALOG OPPORTUNITIES IN THE AI ERA - ADI combines advanced power conversion, intelligent system control and real-time telemetry for next-generation processors operating at 6,000 A and sub-1V. Framing on efficiency: a 97% converter loses roughly 50% more energy as heat than a 98% one, compounding into cooling infrastructure and opex.
800V->intermediate: 20 kW at >2.5 kW/cubic inch; core rails 6,000 A at sub-1V; >98% efficiency

Empower Semiconductor acquisition CLOSED July 7, 2026 for $1.5 BILLION in an all-cash transaction, extending ADI's vertical power story by taking power INTO THE PROCESSOR PACKAGE itself. In large-scale AI deployments the architecture reduces compute power consumption and temperature by approximately 10%-15%, equating to roughly $30 MILLION IN ANNUAL SAVINGS IN A 1 GW DATA CENTER. Cash and short-term investments fell to $2.3B on the close; net leverage ratio now 0.9.
Empower closed 07-07-2026 for $1.5B cash; -10-15% compute power/temp; ~$30M/yr saved per 1GW DC

GRID-TO-CHIP strategy: data center capacity is now measured in GIGAWATTS rather than FLOPS/TOPS and POWER AVAILABILITY HAS BECOME THE PRIMARY CONSTRAINT TO FURTHER AI PROGRESS. ADI supplies grid monitoring (real-time voltage, current, power quality, system health) to utilities, energy operators and infrastructure providers, plus battery management for energy storage - one of the grid's fastest-growing sectors. To accelerate time-to-power, hyperscalers are increasingly exploring DEDICATED MICROGRIDS, opening additional growth avenues that augment ADI's $500M+ energy business (inflected in 2025, accelerating in 2026). ADI now spans the entire electricity value chain: generation, transmission, storage, distribution, rack power and ultimately processor power delivery - 'essentially the vascular system of the data center.'
Energy business $500M+, inflected 2025 and accelerating in 2026; microgrid opportunity

2030 SAM RESET: ADI's current assessment is that its 2030 data center AND energy SAM has MORE THAN DOUBLED versus what it envisioned just one year ago - driven not simply by higher AI infrastructure CapEx but by new markets and architectures requiring ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE MORE ANALOG CONTENT delivered via higher-value solutions. Supporting math from the call: ~100 GW equivalent of data center infrastructure is expected to be built between now and 2031, with EACH GIGAWATT generating a $1B-$1.5B analog SAM. Runway seen extending to at least 2030 for strong double-digit data center growth; the ~$0.5B energy business is expected to DOUBLE by the end of the decade. ADI is contemplating long-term company growth above the 5%-7% model set at its 2021 investor day.
2030 DC+energy SAM >2x prior view; ~100GW to 2031 at $1-1.5B analog SAM per GW; energy to 2x by 2030

THREE-TIER DEAL MODEL made explicit. (1) MID-TERM core AI cloud contracts of one to three years — four landmark deals closed in Q2 with REFLECTION, COHERE, an unnamed scale U.S. Neolab and a large U.S.-based quant trading firm, averaging MORE THAN $1B EACH at a yield of $20-25M PER MEGAWATT, upfront payments covering 50-60% of associated capex and payback under two years. (2) SHORT-DURATION capacity of up to six months for time-boxed needs (large training runs before a model release, RL post-training sprints) on dedicated GB300 clusters, being negotiated at $40-50M PER MEGAWATT 'and sometimes above' — roughly double the mid-term yield; one such deal signed recently. (3) LONG-TERM contracts with investment-grade customers, used primarily to finance the build-out. FIRST CAPACITY AUCTION as a price-discovery mechanism: it cleared at the highest price Nebius has ever seen for the BLACKWELL generation — 15% ABOVE THE HIGHEST PRICE IT HAD EVER CHARGED and 20% ABOVE its Blackwell pipeline pricing. Both the auction and the short-term scale-training deals remain take-or-pay, use only a small portion of total capacity, and have faster close-to-deployment cycles. On competitive entry (xAI selling compute at premium prices), CEO Arkady Volozh said new entrants 'validate the market' — the AI cloud market is growing tens of gigawatts per year while Nebius plans roughly 1 GW per year, so hyperscalers 'cannot build all of it'.
first auction cleared 15% above highest price ever charged, 20% above Blackwell pipeline
